fields.summary: Autonomous plan of the bug where a reviser session's 'python3 -m json.tool .rhiza/log/<cs>/*.json' wrote one entry over another, broke PR #457's lint, and was repaired by hand from the persistent index. The planner read the code: rhiza writes entries via temp file + link (internal/store/store.go writeNew, mode 0644); every agent session already has a PreToolUse hook (rhiza session hook, claudecode adapter); every run commit step (build/review/ship-change render steps, plan gate 'Render the plan', ship land, ship rebase) runs rhiza render first, and render reads the whole log but ignores its problems; the index's entries table keeps each good entry's canonical bytes and never re-reads a seen path. No owner took part. The planner asked one question with three parts (how to guard, where to refuse, what repair looks like); the arbiter answered with Decision decision-log-guard (assumed, would have escalated): entries written 0444 and re-moded by render, plus a PreToolUse deny of Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit under .rhiza/log/ with no shell parsing; render fails naming each non-canonical, misnamed or HEAD-changed entry; a new rhiza repair (with --dry-run) restores from HEAD or the index entries table; guidance says to read entries with rhiza show/slice or cat. The change set serves m4-runs-hold-up, as runs must finish without hand repair.
fields.title: Plan interview: guarding the log against agent overwrites (autonomous)
